newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed mostly lower on origin selling. November shed $29 to close at $1,510 a tonne, while second month January lost $40 to close at $1,384 a tonne. In New York arabica futures ended sharply lower battered by a round of profit taking. The market had a strong opening on news Brazil has virtually sold all its 69,000 bags of coffee on offer at an auction but then prices eased on speculative and local selling. The decline occurred simultaneously with an announcement from the CSCE that the drawdown of 24,391 bags in US certified coffee stocks for the week ended October 18 was incorrect due to errors by a warehouse in their reporting. However, the final total of 5,583 bags reported by the Exchange was correct. In other words, this was simply an adjustment in the pace of weekly drawdowns but not in the final total. The Exchange has not provided the final drawdown numbers, but as the total is correct, this should have not any impact on prices. News that Colombian truckers agreed to end a eleven day strike could weigh on prices on Friday. However, as long as the nearby tightness prevails, the market will remain highly nervous.

COLOMBIA - Colombian truckers struck a deal with the government and transport companies to end an eleven day strike that has paralyzed key sectors of the economy. The compromise grants an immediate 16 per cent rise in cargo freight rates with a further index-linked increase at the start of 1997. A multi-agency commission will be created to carry out a cost study of the industry and introduce possible further reforms. Analysts doubt that the end of the strike will bring instant relief to the hard-hit coffee industry. Private coffee exporters said earlier that even if the strike ended before the weekend there would be significant delays in exports because of the backlocks that have buildup since the stoppage began at midnight October 13.

CANADA - Canada imported 239,449 bags of coffee in May 1996, 0.7 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.139 million bags, 13 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 11 per cent to 2.510 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1996 were Guatemala (118,600 vs 87,800 bags), Mexico (134,100 vs 65,900 bags) and Colombia (200,600 vs 144,800 bags). The country exported 134,900 bags of coffee in January/May 1996, 6 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 9 per cent to 303,800 bags.

SPAIN - Spain imported 341,204 bags of coffee in June 1996, roughly 1 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.839 million bags, 6 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 2.2 per cent to 3.225 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Uganda (509,600 vs 351,700 bags), Brazil (138,300 vs 323,100 bags), Colombia (193,100 vs 176,400 bags) and Vietnam (121,400 vs 145,800 bags). The country exported 252,100 bags of coffee in January/June 1996, 26 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 6.7 per cent to 401,000 bags.
